About AI discoveries in 2020

This selection contains 289 catalog entries dated 1 Jan 2020 to 30 Dec 2020. 289 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

24 Dec 2020Brigham and Women's Hospital; Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School

Topic models reveal differing clinical-note trajectories around vasculitis treatment

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An unsupervised analysis of 113,048 notes from 660 vasculitis patients found differing documentation trajectories around treatment initiation. Kidney-inflammation mentions peaked near treatment start, whereas other manifestations were more persistent; psychiatric symptoms also appeared before treatment. These are patterns in documentation, not measured disease incidence or causal treatment effects.

Technology: Latent Dirichlet allocation with cross-run topic stabilization

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Unsupervised learned word-topic distributions expose documentation themes and temporal contrasts that would be missed by restricting analysis to structured codes.
Test and result
Three learned 100-topic models yielded 90 stable topics, which two vasculitis experts independently labeled and reconciled. Notes were aligned from two years before to five years after treatment in three-month windows. Topics for glomerulonephritis peaked near treatment initiation while pulmonary and other symptom mentions persisted. Source-reported correlations with structured-data trends were .80 for treatment and .92 for glomerulonephritis.
Limitation / still unknown
This is one retrospective healthcare-system cohort of prevalent PR3/MPO-ANCA-positive cases, with no non-vasculitis comparator or independent clinical validation. Before-treatment notes were fewer and involved fewer patients. Topic scores are fractions of assigned words within pooled documentation windows, not patient risks or incidence; copy-and-paste, templates, note density and outside-system care can affect trends. Psychiatric symptoms and diagnostic delays were already known in vasculitis; this analysis does not establish their first discovery. No causal treatment effect or prospective diagnostic performance is shown.

24 Dec 2020School of Surveying and Landing Information Engineering, Henan Polytechnic University, Jiaozuo 454000, China

Improving the Resolution and Accuracy of Groundwater Level Anomalies Using the Machine Learning-Based Fusion Model in the North China Plain

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning fusion system downscaled GRACE water-storage observations and combined groundwater, precipitation, runoff and evapotranspiration data to estimate groundwater-level anomalies in China’s North China Plain. Against six in-situ datasets, the prediction module improved average correlation from 0.43 to 0.71; transfer beyond the study area was not shown.

Technology: A machine-learning fusion/downscaling model estimates groundwater-level anomalies and compares them with observed water levels.

23 Dec 2020Carnegie Mellon University

Autonomous machine-learning experiments identify a dual-anion aqueous sodium electrolyte with a wider stability window

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3. On platinum, the blend had a wider electrochemical stability window than the NaClO4 baseline despite lower total salt concentration; follow-up tests reported a 24 mV increase in the OER potential at the stated leakage-current criterion and 58% lower current density at 2 V. The result is a measured electrolyte formulation under the paper’s electrochemical protocols, not evidence of a commercial battery or field-ready cell.

Technology: Dragonfly Bayesian optimization software coupled to the Otto robotic electrochemistry test stand

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Dragonfly selected electrolyte formulations sequentially from real-time measurements and guided autonomous experiment requests to Otto; the paper reports the mixed-anion sodium formulation as the optimization result.
Test and result
A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3.
Limitation / still unknown
The study measured electrochemical behavior primarily on platinum electrodes and reports a wider stability window for the selected aqueous blend under its stated protocol. This does not establish long-term performance, commercial readiness, or general improvement across battery chemistries.

PET and MRI learning classifies prostate lesion risk

Test and result
The six-hospital cohort had 820 admission examinations, with outcomes classified as mild versus non-invasive ventilation, intensive care or death. Training-fold normalization, feature selection and parameter fitting were described. In original v1 Table 5, GoogleNet image features plus clinical data and logistic regression achieved mean accuracy .743±.061, sensitivity .769±.189 and specificity .685±.155 across held-out centers; clinical-data SVM accuracy was .734±.044. The later August 2021 journal tables retain these values.

Many configurations were compared, and displayed best performances do not constitute an untouched locked-model evaluation. Severe outcome combines several care decisions and mortality; the results do not establish time-to-event prognosis, treatment effect, capacity improvement or clinically significant added value over records alone. The v1 archive says submitted December 11, 2020, while its PDF carries a December 14 version header; this entry uses the dated PDF version and does not assert a first-public-day priority. Journal publication was August 28, 2021.

6 Dec 2020Princeton University; DeepMind; New York University; Flatiron Institute; Carnegie Mellon University

AI-derived symbolic formula improves dark-matter halo overdensity estimates in a cosmological simulation

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A graph neural network trained on a detailed N-body cosmological dark-matter simulation was distilled by symbolic regression into an analytic estimator for a halo’s overdensity from its mass and the masses, positions and velocities of nearby halos. On the analyzed simulation snapshot, the new expression reduced mean absolute error to 0.0882, compared with 0.121 for the authors’ existing hand-designed estimator. The formula’s mass-weighted neighborhood term decreases with separation and includes dependence on the central halo’s mass.

Technology: Sparse-representation Graph Neural Network followed by Eureqa genetic-programming symbolic regression

Editorial relevance 40 astronomy Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The team trained a graph neural network to predict dark-matter halo overdensity using a cosmological N-body simulation. L1 regularization encouraged a compact learned message representation; Eureqa symbolic regression then fitted explicit equations to the learned graph-network components and replaced them with a closed-form model. This process yielded a previously unreported analytic halo-environment estimator and enabled comparison against the existing hand-designed formula.
Test and result
A graph neural network trained on a detailed N-body cosmological dark-matter simulation was distilled by symbolic regression into an analytic estimator for a halo’s overdensity from its mass and the masses, positions and velocities of nearby halos.
Limitation / still unknown
The formula was derived and evaluated on a single final-time-step dataset from an N-body simulation (215,854 halos), not validated against observations or independent cosmological simulations. The authors note that some terms’ physical interpretation was unclear and reserved detailed interpretation for future astrophysics work. It is a new useful estimator for the studied simulated halo population, not a confirmed universal law of dark-matter structure.

Early cardiac MRI images identify pleural effusions in retrospective testing

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An adapted HRNet segmented early anatomical cardiac MRI images and quantified pleural fluid. In a 200-scan test set containing 42 report-positive effusions, fluid quantification distinguished report-positive scans with an AUC of 0.906. Adaptive scanning and patient benefits were proposed rather than tested.

Technology: HRNet convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
An adapted HRNet learned pixel labels from clinician annotations; segmented slices were reconstructed into a 3D fluid volume used to distinguish report-positive pleural effusions.
Test and result
Retrospective 575-scan study across two hospitals and two scanner manufacturers: 375 scans for training/validation and 200 for testing. Clinicians labelled 1,500 development slices. HRNet segmentation and 3D fluid quantification yielded pleural-effusion AUC 0.906 against final clinical reports; 42 of 200 test scans had reported effusions.
Limitation / still unknown
Report-based reference rather than an independently adjudicated effusion standard; no prospective workflow or patient-benefit test. Generalization beyond these centers remains uncertain. Separate chamber-size claims require manufacturer-specific regression calibration whose fitting partition is unclear, and are not represented here. Threshold-specific accuracy is omitted because optimal cut-offs were evaluated in the study dataset.

AI contribution

Test and result
Final models trained on 3160 PRO-ACT patients were compared against observed ALSFRS-R trajectories in 509 patients from a separate completed olesoxime trial. Limitation / still unknown
Both datasets were existing clinical-trial records. Prediction became poorer farther from baseline, and results do not establish treatment-effect estimation or patient benefit. A simulated16% effective-sample-size gain under a hypothetical treatment effect is not an observed clinical-trial gain. Random-forest and ensemble models do not explicitly account for within-person longitudinal correlation; missing-at-random assumptions may fail outside these data.

27 Aug 2020Fraunhofer Research Institution for Marine Biotechnology and Cell Technology; University of Lübeck; University Hospital Leipzig; Medical Laser Center Lübeck; University of Warwick

EntireAxon reveals coexisting patterns of axonal degeneration in a cell-culture model

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Initially reported in an August 2020 preprint and subsequently journal-published in 2021, EntireAxon combined neural image segmentation and temporal classification to track cortical axons in an in-vitro hemorrhagic-stroke model. The study found that axonal swellings preceded fragmentation and that granular, retraction, swelling and transport patterns could occur together. The finding is limited to unmyelinated axons and hemin exposure; small image-label validation sets, weak fragment segmentation and absent in-vivo confirmation limit generalization.

Technology: EntireAxon U-Net/ResNet-50 segmentation ensemble; attention-based recurrent neural network

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The CNN segments axon structures in time-lapse images; the RNN learns temporal changes in segmentation-class histograms. These operations provide the measurements and pattern classifications used for the new in-vitro biological finding.
Test and result
A U-Net/ResNet-50 ensemble learned pixel classes for background, axons, swellings and fragments from 33 labeled images and was compared with human labels on eight validation images. Its segmentation quantified newly recorded degeneration time courses from six independent cortical-neuron cultures per condition. An RNN analyzed temporal class transitions and was checked with ten-fold cross-validation over 162 labeled examples, supporting the finding that four degeneration patterns coexist and swellings precede fragmentation.
Limitation / still unknown
The CNN fragment-class F1 was only 0.301 and the validation labels shared an annotator with the training labels. RNN folds were not established as independent by culture/biological replicate in the reviewed Methods. The source limits the biology to unmyelinated cultured axons and hemin-induced injury, notes that other hemorrhage products may differ, and does not establish in-vivo mechanisms or clinical benefit.

Four machine-learning classifiers jointly ranked candidate transit signals against planet and false-positive scenarios. A Gaussian-process classifier, supported by random-forest, extra-trees and multilayer-perceptron models, was applied to Kepler transit candidates.

The 50 are statistically validated candidates from archival Kepler observations, not newly observed planets. An Artificial Intelligence Characterised Functional Ingredient, Derived from Rice, Inhibits TNF-α and Significantly Improves Physical Strength in an Inflammaging Population.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An ensemble of ten neural networks predicted anti-inflammatory rice peptides, which were identified in a rice peptide hydrolysate and tested in vitro. A 12-week pilot randomized 40 older adults (30 rice NPN, 10 placebo); its primary digestive-discomfort endpoint was not met, while secondary physical-performance and biomarker outcomes favored treatment. Small sample, compliance/timing confounding, and the ingredient-versus-isolated-peptide distinction limit inference.

Technology: Trained neural-network ensemble for peptide bioactivity prediction

Editorial relevance 47 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A ten-model neural-network ensemble predicted anti-inflammatory peptides from food proteomes and helped characterize peptides detected in rice NPN; peptide and ingredient effects were then tested by mass spectrometry, cell assays, and a human pilot. The AI prediction itself did not establish clinical effect.
Test and result
Eight predicted peptides were synthesized; seven reduced TNF-α secretion in stimulated THP-1 assays. A 12-week pilot randomized 40 older adults (rice NPN 30, placebo 10). The digestive-discomfort primary endpoint was not met; secondary chair-stand/SPPB results favored treatment. Figure captions report at least 27/10 and 28/10 analyzed for those outcomes, respectively.
Limitation / still unknown
The pilot was small and randomized 30:10; the primary subjective endpoint was not met, and authors noted compliance and Christmas-period measurement as confounders. The clinical intervention was a rice peptide hydrolysate, so effects cannot be assigned to individual AI-predicted peptides. Clinical efficacy and generalizability need confirmation.

31 Jul 2020Mediterranea Cardiocentro; IRCCS Neuromed; CORIST collaboration

A random forest ranks mortality-associated markers in the Italian CORIST cohort

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An exploratory random forest analysis of 3,894 hospitalized COVID-19 patients ranked renal function, C-reactive protein and age as influential mortality-classification features. Conventional survival analyses in the same cohort supported associated risks. These retrospective findings are neither causal effects nor an independently validated clinical risk tool.

Technology: Random forest, permutation feature importance and k-nearest-neighbor imputation

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned forest and permutation analysis provided an exploratory nonlinear feature ranking; conventional survival modeling supplied complementary association estimates. Their agreement is not independent confirmation.
Test and result
The retrospective 30-center Italian cohort included 3,894 patients admitted from February 19 to May 23, 2020; 712 died and 532 were still hospitalized at the May 29 cutoff. RF development used 2,725 patients and a random 1,169-patient test subset, with training hyperparameter search. Renal function and C-reactive protein ranked above age in the reported feature-importance analysis; conventional Cox models analyzed associations with time to in-hospital death.
Limitation / still unknown
Imputation and normalization are described before the train/test split, without clear fold-specific fitting. Although Methods discuss test-set importance, the primary figure caption places the permutation-importance analysis in the training sample; this record does not claim independently reproduced feature rankings. The test subset came from the same pooled cohort, not a new hospital or external population. Ongoing hospitalization at cutoff complicates a binary death/no-death target. High reported survival sensitivity coexisted with low specificity; overall accuracy is not validated mortality sensitivity. Missing smoking/obesity data, absent vital signs, treatment differences and residual confounding limit interpretation. Cox hazard ratios are conventional same-cohort associations, not AI-derived causal findings.

The 4/5 warning result is cross-validation on this historical record, not independent operational validation; the model was described as a prototype. The proposed hydrothermal charging mechanism is an interpretation of the seismic pattern.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Random-forest analysis of 4,323 Dutch home-care clients found that recorded nursing diagnoses and symptoms added information beyond existing case-mix groups. Reported internal cross-validated R-squared for weekly care hours increased from 22.4% to 32.1% when nursing-record features were added. The result concerns observed service use at one provider, not objectively necessary care or improved payment policy. Documentation differences and underprediction of high-use clients limit generalization.

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Forest ensembles learn interactions among demographic, case-mix and nursing-assessment variables to estimate recorded care-hour use; comparing feature sets measures the information added by nursing records.
Test and result
One randomly selected assessment per client was retained to prevent repeated-client leakage. Forest models were compared using ten-fold validation against average weekly care hours in the 28 days after assessment, with demographic/case-mix and nursing-record feature sets.
Limitation / still unknown
Performance at other providers, clinically appropriate care need and reimbursement-policy effects remain unestablished. The primary body describes feature elimination but its exact nesting/tuning details are in an unreviewed supplement. Care hours combine nursing and personal care, and documentation practices can vary.

Test and result
A feature-restricted GBM was retrained on ADNI to match available AddNeuroMed measurements, retaining thirty-two clinical, imaging and genetic features. No clinical prevention, treatment selection, economic benefit or general-population diagnostic utility was demonstrated.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

AI contribution
A random survival forest selects prognostic immune-related genes after Cox screening; the selected genes define the survival-risk score whose associations and immune profiles are tested in archived clinical datasets.
Test and result
GSE31210 supplied 204 discovery patients; GSE41271 and GSE50081 supplied 309 validation patients, and TCGA supplied 441. Cox screening followed by random-survival-forest selection produced twelve genes for a Cox-weighted score. Limitation / still unknown
Each validation cohort used its own median cutoff, so this is not locked-threshold clinical validation. Internal comparisons found closer perfusion-deficit measurements to the full acquisitions than the uncorrected shortened data. These are image-based clinical measurement results, without independently acquired short-scan validation, established diagnostic accuracy or demonstrated radiation-dose benefit.

Technology: Twenty-layer dilated residual convolutional neural networks for projection-domain SPECT reconstruction

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned residual networks restored projection information before reconstruction, enabling the represented within-cohort test of clinical perfusion-measurement agreement under reduced data.
Test and result
A prospectively collected 363-person clinical cohort supplied full-acquisition list-mode data. Shorter-time data used the first half of acquisition events, while fewer-projection data omitted alternate views. Residual networks learned projection restoration; the source describes tenfold cross-validation on the cohort. Reconstructed clinical perfusion measures, including total perfusion deficit, were compared with full acquisitions using commercial quantitative software and agreement analyses. Learned reconstructions reduced measured bias relative to uncorrected reduced data.
Limitation / still unknown
Reduced acquisitions were derived from the same full scans, rather than separate real-world short scans. Full-acquisition reconstruction is a measurement reference, not independent disease truth. Detailed fold-specific preprocessing/tuning isolation is not established. Gated functional performance, diagnostic decisions, patient outcomes and actual lower-dose acquisition were not tested. Some headline image-metric labels and dispersion values are inconsistent, so they are not adopted as precise comparative claims.

Test and result
Baseline face-processing fMRI and available two-year follow-up identified 39 rapid-remission, 31 gradual-improvement and 15 chronic-course patients. Source footnotes warn that McNemar comparisons between cross-validated classifiers may be optimistic. The original preprint API dates version1 to September 18, 2019; only its metadata/abstract were available in this review, so journal-specific metrics are not backdated. No individualized-treatment benefit or causal neural mechanism is established.
